fix: Make retro's dispatch path produce a phasestream events file under one of the two surveyed names (retro-events.ndjson or retrospective-events.ndjson), the same stream every runner-dispatched phase gets. Root the fix at the dispatch call in internal/core/failure_learning.go (retro dispatches outside the runner path that wires phasestream). Wiring proof: after the fix, `evolve cycle outputs <N>` on a retro cycle must survey 0 gaps for retro, and the phase-outputs-surveyed event for that cycle must drop the retro gap. Do NOT exempt retro in phaseoutputs instead — the gap is real and the register requires live evidence of legitimate non-production, which this is not.
notes: Found by adversarial review of the phase-output tracker (feat/phase-output-monitoring). Until fixed, every retro cycle's survey reports exactly one known gap: 'retro: retro-events.ndjson missing' — disclosed in the wave protocol, intentionally NOT exempted.
summary: Retro produces NO phasestream events file in any live workspace (verified cycles 1432/1441/1442: retro-observer-events.ndjson exists but is the observer's stream, a different mechanism; neither retro-events.ndjson nor retrospective-events.ndjson exists). Retro dispatches outside the runner path (runner.go sets Agent=phase and phasestream keys on it), so its prompt is agent-named (retrospective-prompt.txt) and its events stream was simply never wired. A reviewer of a FAIL cycle's retro therefore cannot replay what the retro agent did — exactly the 'not enough data for review' class the phase-output tracker exists to surface.
title: Retro phase produces no events stream — its dispatch path never wired phasestream
